title: Add staggered admission failsafe and transparent regional bridge
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed two related failure modes during the outage window on 2026-02-08: abrupt full-tenant admission drops when an overloaded regional slowpath flipped circuits, and a correlated KV-cache pressure that caused long tail latency during rapid tenant replays. This PR introduces a coordinated, telemetry-driven 'staggered admission' failsafe plus a transparent regional-bridge that keeps traffic flowing via a lightweight forwarding path while preserving KV-coherency and SLO accounting.

Summary of changes: 1) admission_controller: implement a two-stage admit ramp (soft-reject -> graded-queue -> normal) with epoched tokens per tenant; 2) bridge_manager: new transparent bridge mode that can forward select routes to a warm standby region while preserving KV drain ordering; 3) telemetry: add bridging and admit-stage metrics + redo existing SLO counters so the SLO enforcer charges tenants correctly during staged admission; 4) hotfix utilities: kv-drain helper script and a short rollout playbook.

Why this is different: Unlike previous blunt load-shed patches, the staggered admit preserves request shaping — short requests and health-checks still pass in early stages while heavy batched jobs are deferred. The transparent bridge keeps clients online by routing to compatible model variants in a standby region without requiring DNS flips or long failover windows. Both are designed to be reversible with a single controller flag.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc updated (docs/ops/regional-bridge.md) - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Telemetry added and validated in staging - [x] Rollout plan written and exercised in canary - [x] Post-merge incident playbook attached

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover admit token lifecycles and queue transitions. Integration E2E simulates elevated latency in region A and asserts the bridge activates, KV-drain script preserves write-order, and SLO billing tags are applied (SLO tag emitted: admission_stage=soft). Staging rollout executed against two tenants with synthetic spike on 2026-02-11. Observed 3-5% higher latency for degraded requests but 99.9% successful responses vs previous 15% error rate.

Rollout strategy: 1) feature flag off in main; 2) enable central controller in staging for 24h with canary tenants; 3) enable bridge passive mode (no traffic forwarding) and assert metrics; 4) flip to active for 1% traffic with slow ramp; 5) monitor SLO / KV pressure dashboards for 1h buckets; 6) incremental increase to 25% then full. Backout is a single flag revert and a forced kv-drain abort if bridge misbehaves.

Backward compatibility: New admit stages are additive; default behaviour unchanged. Bridge only forwards routes if a model compatibility predicate is satisfied. No client-visible API changes.

Related work: complements ENG-4401 (proactive-slowpath-prefetch) and SRE-119 (regional failover runbook).

Notes for on-call: run scripts/hotfix/kv-drain.sh in the target region before promoting heavy traffic; telemetry metric names: redwood.admit.stage, redwood.bridge.forward_count, redwood.kvdrain.lag_ms.

Merging notes: squash-merged with a short commit message, rollouts coordinated with SRE team and Solutions Engineering.

review_thread: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach. Can we guarantee write-order preservation when the bridge forwards to a standby in a different region? Suggest making kv-drain idempotent and instrumenting per-tenant lag.
Maya Chen: Answered — kv-drain uses per-tenant monotonically increasing drain tokens; the bridge manager attaches the same token before forwarding. Added per-tenant lag metric. See commit d3a0f41.
Priya Kapoor: CI flakes in integration on first run (timeout on E2E). Please add a retry and shorten default simulated timeout so the test is stable in CI.
Maya Chen: Added deterministic retry backoff and shortened simulated network latency in tests. Re-ran CI; integration now stable.
Noah Patel: Approving pending one telemetry naming nit — prefer redwood.bridge.forward_count to be a histogram for burst analysis.
Maya Chen: Switched metric to histogram in bridging_metrics.yaml and updated dashboards.
release_notes: Add staggered admission (soft-reject -> graded-queue) and a reversible transparent regional bridge to reduce errors during regional slowpath overloads. Includes KV-drain utility, telemetry, and an ops runbook. Enabled behind feature flag.
post_merge_actions: Create canary dashboard with redwood.admit.stage and redwood.bridge.forward_count histograms
Coordinate 2-hour maintenance window for tenant ramp in US-EAST
Tag support cases that observed the Feb 8 outage and notify customers about improved graceful-degradation behavior
